source_note: Source-grounded practice MCQs generated from text-bearing PDFs, DOCX and PPTX course files bundled in the repository. Image-only PDFs were skipped and no OCR was performed. Existing real questions were reused where available. Question-level topic tags are metadata; the current quiz UI does not filter by them yet.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "If these two electrons have opposite spins so that they can occupy the same region (______), both electrons can now preferentially occupy the region between the two nuclei, because they are attracted by both nuclei."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: If these two electrons have opposite spins so that they can occupy the same region (orbital), both electrons can now preferentially occupy the region between the two nuclei, because they are attracted by both nuclei. The missing term is 'orbital'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Identify the element, or elements possible, given only the number of electrons in the outermost shell and the principal ______ of that shell."

questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: (b) Write the allowed number of orbitals (1) with the quantum numbers n = 4, l = 3; (2) with the quantum number n = 4; (3) with the quantum numbers n = 4, l = 2, ml = 0; (4) with the quantum numbers n = 6, l = 5. The missing term is 'quantum number'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "A neutral lithium atom, Li, contains three protons in its nucleus and three electrons, with its outermost electron in the 2s ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: A neutral lithium atom, Li, contains three protons in its nucleus and three electrons, with its outermost electron in the 2s orbital. The missing term is 'orbital'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Proper ______ precautions must be taken to ensure that the radionuclides produced are always contained within vessels from which neither they nor their radiations can escape."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Proper shielding precautions must be taken to ensure that the radionuclides produced are always contained within vessels from which neither they nor their radiations can escape. The missing term is 'shielding'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Therefore, any atomic ______ can be populated by only zero, one, or two electrons."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Therefore, any atomic orbital can be populated by only zero, one, or two electrons. The missing term is 'orbital'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "We defined ______ as the tendency of an atom to attract electrons to itself in a chemical bond."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: We defined electronegativity as the tendency of an atom to attract electrons to itself in a chemical bond. The missing term is 'electronegativity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "As you recall, an isolated hydrogen atom has the ground state ______ 1s1, with the probability density for this one electron spherically distributed about the hydrogen nucleus."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: As you recall, an isolated hydrogen atom has the ground state electron configuration 1s1, with the probability density for this one electron spherically distributed about the hydrogen nucleus. The missing term is 'electron configuration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "In other words, a ______ forms when there are not enough electrons for each individual atom to have a complete octet."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: In other words, a covalent bond forms when there are not enough electrons for each individual atom to have a complete octet. The missing term is 'covalent bond'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Lithium, sodium, and potassium, elements of the leftmost column of the ______ (Group IA), have a single electron in their outermost s orbital (ns1)."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Lithium, sodium, and potassium, elements of the leftmost column of the periodic table (Group IA), have a single electron in their outermost s orbital (ns1). The missing term is 'periodic table'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "(b) The angular momentum (or azimuthal or subsidiary) ______, l, designates the shape of the region in space that an electron occupies."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: (b) The angular momentum (or azimuthal or subsidiary) quantum number, l, designates the shape of the region in space that an electron occupies. The missing term is 'quantum number'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "A disproportionation reaction is a ______ reaction in which the same element is oxidized and reduced."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: A disproportionation reaction is a redox reaction in which the same element is oxidized and reduced. The missing term is 'redox'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Two electrons can occupy the same ______ only if they have opposite spins, ms."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Two electrons can occupy the same orbital only if they have opposite spins, ms. The missing term is 'orbital'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Reduction is a decrease in ______ and corresponds to a gain, or apparent gain, of electrons."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Reduction is a decrease in oxidation number and corresponds to a gain, or apparent gain, of electrons. The missing term is 'oxidation number'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Differentiate between (a) ionic and ______ (b) polar and non-polar covalent bonds giving examples 3."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Differentiate between (a) ionic and covalent bond (b) polar and non-polar covalent bonds giving examples 3. The missing term is 'covalent bond'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The ______, Zeff, experienced by the electron in the 2s orbital, however, is not 1 (3 minus 2) either."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: The effective nuclear charge, Zeff, experienced by the electron in the 2s orbital, however, is not 1 (3 minus 2) either. The missing term is 'effective nuclear charge'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the usual relationship between atomic radius and first ______, other factors being equal?"
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: What is the usual relationship between atomic radius and first ionization energy, other factors being equal? The missing term is 'ionization energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "64 The ______ of fluorine (4.0) is higher than that of any other element."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: 64 The electronegativity of fluorine (4.0) is higher than that of any other element. The missing term is 'electronegativity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "72 The electrons are shared between the two hydrogen atoms, and a single ______ is formed."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: 72 The electrons are shared between the two hydrogen atoms, and a single covalent bond is formed. The missing term is 'covalent bond'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ Metallic bonds join atoms of metals and alloys together."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Metallic bond Metallic bonds join atoms of metals and alloys together. The missing term is 'metallic bond'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The atoms have the (ns)1 ______ and the M+ ions are therefore easily formed."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: The atoms have the (ns)1 electron configuration and the M+ ions are therefore easily formed. The missing term is 'electron configuration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "EXAMPLE Trends in EAs Arrange the following elements in order of increasing values of ______, that is, from most negative to least negative: K, Br, Cs, Cl."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: EXAMPLE Trends in EAs Arrange the following elements in order of increasing values of electron affinity, that is, from most negative to least negative: K, Br, Cs, Cl. The missing term is 'electron affinity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "An electron with 32 electrons will have which principal ______ A."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 2023 Exam PQ.docx: An electron with 32 electrons will have which principal quantum number A. The missing term is 'quantum number'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "But the 3s electron of sodium penetrates the inner shells to a significant extent, so the ______ felt by the outermost (3s) electron is actually greater than it is for lithium (2s)."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: But the 3s electron of sodium penetrates the inner shells to a significant extent, so the effective nuclear charge felt by the outermost (3s) electron is actually greater than it is for lithium (2s). The missing term is 'effective nuclear charge'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The strength of this interaction depends on the charge and size of the ion and on the magnitude of the ______ and size of the molecule."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: The strength of this interaction depends on the charge and size of the ion and on the magnitude of the dipole moment and size of the molecule. The missing term is 'dipole moment'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Figure below shows a plot of ______ versus atomic number for several elements."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Figure below shows a plot of electron affinity versus atomic number for several elements. The missing term is 'electron affinity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Reactions often consist of a sequence of individ ual sub-steps, the so-called elementary reactions, and the information on the precise course of action is part of the ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Reactions often consist of a sequence of individ ual sub-steps, the so-called elementary reactions, and the information on the precise course of action is part of the reaction mechanism. The missing term is 'reaction mechanism'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the usual relationship between nuclear charge and first ______, other factors being equal?"
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: What is the usual relationship between nuclear charge and first ionization energy, other factors being equal? The missing term is 'ionization energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "113 Perhalic Acids and Perhalates The oxyacids containing chlorine and bromine in the +7 ______ are very strong acids."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: 113 Perhalic Acids and Perhalates The oxyacids containing chlorine and bromine in the +7 oxidation state are very strong acids. The missing term is 'oxidation state'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "PERIODIC PROPERTIES OF THE ELEMENTS Now we investigate the nature of ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: PERIODIC PROPERTIES OF THE ELEMENTS Now we investigate the nature of periodicity. The missing term is 'periodicity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Two of such electrons in the same ______ are paired."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Two of such electrons in the same orbital are paired. The missing term is 'orbital'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "So we must learn to recognize, from positions of elements in the periodic table and known trends in ______, when the difference in electronegativity is large enough to favor ionic bonding."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: So we must learn to recognize, from positions of elements in the periodic table and known trends in electronegativity, when the difference in electronegativity is large enough to favor ionic bonding. The missing term is 'electronegativity'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The second ______ value is generally much larger than the first ionization energy."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: The second ionization energy value is generally much larger than the first ionization energy. The missing term is 'ionization energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Only valence electrons are shown in a ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: Only valence electrons are shown in a Lewis structure. The missing term is 'Lewis structure'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "For calcium, for example, the first ______, IE1, is 590 kJ/mol: The second ionization energy (IE2) is the amount of energy required to remove the second electron."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: For calcium, for example, the first ionization energy, IE1, is 590 kJ/mol: The second ionization energy (IE2) is the amount of energy required to remove the second electron. The missing term is 'ionization energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "For example, tungsten for use in light bulb filaments can be prepared by reduction of tungsten(VI) oxide with hydrogen at 1200°C: Tungsten is reduced, and its ______ decreases from +6 to zero."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 121 NOTES.pdf: For example, tungsten for use in light bulb filaments can be prepared by reduction of tungsten(VI) oxide with hydrogen at 1200°C: Tungsten is reduced, and its oxidation state decreases from +6 to zero. The missing term is 'oxidation state'.
